title: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment Act, 2023 - ABS Compliance
authority: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) & State Biodiversity Boards (SBB)
official_citation: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (Act 18 of 2003) & Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023
summary: Mandates Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) compliance for commercial utilization of biological resources occurring in India and prior approval before applying for intellectual property rights based on Indian bio-resources.
key_clauses: Section 6(1): No person shall apply for any intellectual property right, by whatever name called, in or outside India for any invention based on any research or information on a biological resource obtained from India without obtaining prior approval of National Biodiversity Authority (Form III).
Section 3 & 4: Non-Indian citizens, foreign-controlled companies, or foreign collaborations require Form I NBA approval prior to accessing Indian bio-resources.

2023 Amendment Relief: Codified traditional knowledge practitioners, Ayush practitioners, and cultivators of medicinal plants are exempted from intimation to SBB, BUT patent applications still require NBA approval under Section 6.
ABS Benefit Sharing Fee: Typically 0.1% to 0.5% of ex-factory sale price or 3.0% to 5.0% of upfront patent licensing royalty paid to NBA.
practical_guidance: File Form III with the National Biodiversity Authority at least 6-12 months prior to patent grant. Grant of patent by Indian Patent Office will be withheld or kept in abeyance without NBA NOC.

title: Plant Variety Protection & Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
authority: PPV&FR Authority, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
official_citation: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 (Act 53 of 2001)
summary: Grants plant breeders' rights for novel, distinct, uniform, and stable (DUS) varieties of medicinal and aromatic plants while safeguarding farmers' traditional rights to save, use, sow, and exchange seed.
key_clauses: Medicinal plant cultivars (e.g. high-withanolide Ashwagandha cultivars like NMITLI-118, high-curcumin Turmeric IISR Prabha) can be registered under PPV&FR.
Section 39(1)(iv): Farmers are protected from infringement if they innocent of the law or cultivating for non-commercial farm-saved seeds.
Registration provides 15 years protection for extant varieties and 18 years for trees/vines.
practical_guidance: Ayurvedic cultivators and agricultural startups should protect newly bred high-yielding chemotype varieties via PPV&FR registration rather than patenting the whole plant (barred under Indian Patent Act Section 3(j)).
